name: Susan Guzick
title: Counsellor (ACA Level 4)
description: Hello, I’m Sue. People I work with include those who have complex experiences of depression, PTSD, neurodiversity, social anxiety, family violence, trauma, chronic physical conditions, cognition and memory impacts, personality disorders, schizophrenia, hoarding experiences, alcohol or drug use, and isolation. My qualifications include the Master of Art Therapy (integrated Counselling), Dip of Mental Health, ongoing Master of Counselling, and specialised training with complex mental health and trauma. Evidence-base methods can include Interpersonal Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Trauma / Poly-Vagal Theory, Internal Family Systems, and Art Therapy Expressive methods.

name: Tailah Walker-Cuman
title: Counsellor (ACA Level 1)
description: Tailah Cuman is a holistic counsellor specialising in emotional neglect. She has traveled internationally delivering workshops on emotions, movement and the nervous system. Her clientele generally consists of people under 40 who have experienced varying degrees of emotional neglect or developmental trauma, and whom have tried regular psychology or counselling but have not seen the mental, emotional and spiritual relief they are after.

description: It can be hard to consider coming to therapy… You might be experiencing chronic pain or recurring physical symptoms. Perhaps you are exhausted and you feel like you have already tried everything. Maybe you are worried or overwhelmed by the relationships in your life.

name: Tim Fraser
title: Counsellor (ACA Level 2)
description: I support clients with a range of issues, but I am particularly focused on the role of attachment and how developing a secure attachment style can help heal various issues. I completed a Graduate Diploma in psychology at the University of Melbourne, then trained in integrative Psychotherapy at the Ikon institute of Australia. I’ve studied mentalisation-based therapy, different meta-cognitive therapies, and Psychodynamic Interpersonal Therapy (The Conversational Model), but I also frequently draw on Internal Family Systems, somatic experiencing, and cognitive-behavioural therapy.
